summary: This article explains why our bodies make us yawn and hiccup, and what scientists think causes these strange, involuntary habits.
introduce: Draw a simple cause → effect arrow on the board and ask students for an everyday example, such as “I did not sleep, so I felt tired.” Tell them that while reading “Why We Yawn and Hiccup” they will find at least two cause-and-effect links.

keyTerms.def: able to spread easily from one person to another
a sudden, uncontrolled tightening of a muscle
to cause something to start happening

challengeTerms.def: happening automatically, without a person choosing or controlling it
an automatic action the body performs without conscious thought
an idea that a scientist proposes and then tests to see if it is correct

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that yawning and hiccups are just silly habits with no real purpose? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how yawning and hiccups are alike and different.
struggling: Pre-teach contagious, spasm, and trigger with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses involuntary, reflex, and hypothesis to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
